sentences.text:
on 4 September, 2025
 The Hon'Ble Smt.Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 Criminal Petition No.9241 of 2025
Order:

-
1. This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS),
2023 seeking to quash the proceedings against the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 6 in S.C.No.635 of 2023, on the file of the learned Special Sessions Judge FTC for Atrocities against Women, at Hyderabad, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 417, 420, 376, 294-B, 509 and 506 IPC.
2.

entities.text: Special Sessions Judge FTC for Atrocities against Women
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Sri C.Praveen Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners/accused Nos. 1 to 6 as well as Sri Jitender Rao Veeramalla, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent No.1-State.

3. When the matter is taken up for hearing, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that though the parties have attempted to compromise the matter, they did not appear before the Secretary, High Court Legal Services Committee for identification.
Hence, sought a direction to dispense with the appearance of the petitioners before the Trial Court.
4. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that appropriate orders may be passed.

The allegations leveled against the petitioners are under Sections 417, 420,
376, 294(b), 509 and 506 IPC.
S.C.No.635 of 2023 is pending on the file of the learned Special Sessions Judge FTC for Atrocities against women, Hyderabad.
Truth or otherwise of the said allegations can be brought out during the course of trial.
This Court is not inclined to interfere with the judicial process.
6. Hence, the Criminal Petition is disposed of directing the learned Trial Court to dispose of S.C.No.635 of 2023 at the earliest.

However, the presence of the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 6 is dispensed with before the Trial Court provided that the petitioners are represented through an Advocate on every date of hearing and that they shall be present before the Trial Court whenever they are specifically required during the course of trial.
7. Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
